actor.instructions: Whose position or action is expressed in target_statement? For a promise or restriction, identify the party undertaking the action or bound by it. For a concern, identify the actor to whom that concern is attributed. A person reporting another actor’s position is not that actor. Use context to resolve attribution. The report issuer alone does not make every quoted statement a CPC position.

criteria.applicant: The project applicant or developer, including a government agency applying for the project.
criteria.cpc: The City Planning Commission itself, expressing its position or describing its own review or design change.
criteria.community_board: A Community Board, its chair, or its representative.
criteria.council_member_and_board: The concern or position is explicitly attributed jointly to a Council member and Community Board.
criteria.council_body: The City Council acting as a legislative body, not merely an individual member.
criteria.independent_civic: An independent neighborhood, homeowner, advocacy, or civic organization, not an applicant, government agency or Community Board.
criteria.unclear: The supplied statement and context do not identify the responsible actor clearly.

status.instructions: What does target_statement say happened? Classify this statement, not the whole project. Context may establish who spoke or whether this exact rule was accepted. A board recommendation remains a request unless the supplied text explicitly records acceptance of that particular provision. For a declaration rule, distinguish an adopted or signed rule from rule language whose acceptance is not supplied. A conditional rule can be adopted even if the project has not been built.

criteria.concern: An actor explicitly raises a worry, question, objection or concern. An explicitly stated design or preservation concern counts even if it helped shape the original proposal.
criteria.request: An actor asks for an action or recommends a particular provision, including conditions in a Community Board recommendation. Acceptance of that specific provision is not established.
criteria.applicant_promise: The applicant explicitly states that it will do the action. This does not require separate CPC imposition or proof the action was performed.
criteria.adopted_requirement: The exact substantive requirement is imposed by a deciding body or appears in a declaration whose signature or adoption is established in the supplied context. Being conditional on development does not remove it.
criteria.incorporated_change: The report expressly says the design or proposal has been changed or improved, or a specific feature has been ensured through review, without establishing a formal imposed condition.
criteria.proposal_description: A proposed feature is only described; no explicit promise, accepted rule or completed design change is stated.
criteria.support: An actor speaks or acts in favor of the application.
criteria.opposition: An actor speaks or acts against the application.
criteria.main_approval: The deciding body approves the application or main land-use action itself; no separate topic-specific condition is established by this statement.
criteria.no_impact: A routine favorable or no-adverse-impact finding, without a stated concern or request.
criteria.unconfirmed_rule: The statement uses requirement language, but needed evidence that this rule was signed, adopted or accepted is not supplied.
criteria.unclear: The supplied wording does not permit one of these statuses to be determined.

substance.instructions: What kind of action, if any, does target_statement concern? Classify its content independently of whether it was requested, promised or adopted.

criteria.substantive: A specific physical change, provision or restriction, such as planting trees, changing building placement, or limiting parking.
criteria.maintenance: Only routine ongoing maintenance or upkeep, such as maintaining tree pits.
criteria.generic_compliance: Only general compliance with laws or submitted plans, without a particular substantive provision.
criteria.not_an_action: Only a concern, support/opposition, a general approval or a finding; no specific action is requested or undertaken in this statement.

topic_character.instructions: Does target_statement itself discuss neighborhood character, compatibility with surrounding development, preservation of a blockfront, or visual streetscape character. A tree or design feature alone does not establish this topic without such a connection? Use context only to interpret this statement, not to import unrelated topics.

criteria.yes: The target statement addresses this topic.
criteria.no: It does not address this topic.
criteria.unclear: The topic cannot be determined from the supplied wording.

topic_design.instructions: Does target_statement itself discuss physical design or placement of buildings or site features, including a building line, landscaped buffer, or street-tree layout. A garage capacity limit alone is parking, not building design? Use context only to interpret this statement, not to import unrelated topics.

criteria.yes: The target statement addresses this topic.
criteria.no: It does not address this topic.
criteria.unclear: The topic cannot be determined from the supplied wording.

topic_traffic.instructions: Does target_statement itself discuss traffic, congestion, circulation, loading or parking. A vehicle-maintenance facility mentioned only as the approved use does not by itself raise these topics? Use context only to interpret this statement, not to import unrelated topics.

criteria.yes: The target statement addresses this topic.
criteria.no: It does not address this topic.
criteria.unclear: The topic cannot be determined from the supplied wording.

topic_environment.instructions: Does target_statement itself discuss environmental effects, parks, recreation space, landscaping, trees, or green/open space. Include a routine environmental finding as discussion; it does not by itself establish a concern or commitment? Use context only to interpret this statement, not to import unrelated topics.

criteria.yes: The target statement addresses this topic.
criteria.no: It does not address this topic.
criteria.unclear: The topic cannot be determined from the supplied wording.
